content.title: Foam-Stage Type Variant | Adult Gesture, Word Impact and Final Phrase
content.summary: An adult foam-stage choreographer summons short words through steps, arm lifts and a spin before a final phrase. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One clearly adult identity and at least four appearance anchors precede every interface module. + Each module is triggered by one visible body or headphone action and introduces no more than one exact short word. + Waveform, control ring, play bar and fragments remain one coherent graphic system. + Boot and portrait-grid proofs verify the same character before the terminal movement. + The final lockup reunites the adult, settled fragments, recurring rings and one readable original master mark.
quick_start.recommended_input: Establish one original clearly adult animation choreographer with a violet bob, teal headband, cream jacket and cobalt trousers at center stage in a soft coral-and-blue foam-letter room. A two-arm lift raises three blue letters from the floor into the exact short word "UP" while face, headband, jacket and trousers remain unchanged. Her final grounded pose pulls every used letter into one readable foreground phrase "MOVE TOGETHER"; hold the same adult visible above the text and stop all letter motion.
required_anchors: One clearly adult performer, four appearance anchors and one fixed stage axis precede all letter motion.
Each letter group moves only after one corresponding readable dance action begins.
Typography may cross foreground and background but cannot erase performer identity or reset geography.
The final phrase uses the accumulated letters, remains fully readable and shares the frame with the same adult.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: An adult foam-stage choreographer summons short words through steps, arm lifts and a spin before a final phrase. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: 同一明确成年动画舞者在固定彩色黏土舞台上完成连续舞步；散落字母只能在对应动作后弹起、滚动或进入构图，身份与舞台轴线不重置，结尾把全部字母拼成一个清晰原创终句。 The reusable mechanism preserves causal order, spatial anchors and the final proof while replacing every source-specific person, location, object, wording, choreography and design.

invariants.rule: One clearly adult performer, four appearance anchors and one fixed stage axis precede all letter motion.
invariants.purpose: Establishes the baseline identity, object or geography that every later state must preserve.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact baseline rule, later changes cannot be attributed to the same subject, object or place, so the sequence loses its reference state. Removed rule: "One clearly adult performer, four appearance anchors and one fixed stage axis precede all letter motion."

invariants.rule: Each letter group moves only after one corresponding readable dance action begins.
invariants.purpose: Makes the visible trigger precede and explain the first mechanism response.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact trigger rule, the response appears spontaneously and the central cause-and-effect claim is no longer demonstrated. Removed rule: "Each letter group moves only after one corresponding readable dance action begins."

invariants.rule: Every intermediate module introduces at most one exact short word.
invariants.purpose: Keeps the middle progression registered instead of allowing an unexplained reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact progression rule, the middle can jump to a replacement state and the accumulated result is no longer traceable. Removed rule: "Every intermediate module introduces at most one exact short word."

invariants.rule: Typography may cross foreground and background but cannot erase performer identity or reset geography.
invariants.purpose: Reconnects the changed or partial state to the established subject and spatial anchor.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact reconnection rule, detail or transformed shots can belong to a different subject or geography and continuity cannot be verified. Removed rule: "Typography may cross foreground and background but cannot erase performer identity or reset geography."

invariants.rule: The final phrase uses the accumulated letters, remains fully readable and shares the frame with the same adult.
invariants.purpose: Turns the terminal hold into observable proof that the mechanism completed.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact terminal-proof rule, the sequence stops on motion alone and never confirms the promised outcome or preserved aftermath. Removed rule: "The final phrase uses the accumulated letters, remains fully readable and shares the frame with the same adult."
